resources.string: Saved as a .zip file on the BOOT drive of the SD card (the drive every PC sees), in the folder andr36oid-reports

On a PC, open the BOOT drive of the SD card, folder andr36oid-reports, and send the .zip file.

In it: the Android and kernel logs (also from the start before), crash reports, the console model and its DTB, buttons and sticks, battery, temperatures, the SD card, sound and screen, your list of apps, and how many games are in each ROM folder.

Left out: Wi-Fi names and passwords, accounts, contacts, the names of your games and files, serial numbers.

Left out: Wi-Fi names and passwords, accounts, contacts, the names of your games and files, serial numbers. Your list of apps is in it, and the logs can still name Bluetooth devices. Have a look before you post it in public.

On a PC, make a file called make-report.txt on the BOOT drive of the SD card. You can write what went wrong in it. Put the card back and switch on, then wait 5 minutes. The report is saved on BOOT and the file is deleted.
There is no room for it on BOOT, EASYROMS or the internal storage.
